Prayer : Petitions filed under Section 11 of the Contempt of Courts  1971, to punish the respondent for contempt of Court for disobeying  order passed in W.P.No.3165 of 2021 dated 16.11.2021.
For the Petitioner : Ms.David Tyagaraj

For the Respondents : Mr.P.Kumaresan, AGP,
 (for R1 & R2) assisted by  Mr.S.Ravichandran, AGP   Mr.J.Daniel, Govt. Advo  (for R3) : Mr.P.Kumaresan AAG,
 assisted by  Mrs.P.Veena Suresh,
 Standing counsel for CM  ORDER
The contempt petition has been filed to punish the respondents for their wilful disobedience of the orders dated 16.11.2021, passed in W.P.No.3165 of 2021.

2.This Court passed an order on 16.11.2021 as under :
5.The respondents filed a counter stating that the entire acquisition proceedings of the Urban Land Ceiling had passed and attained finality by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in ___________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis SLP Diary No.17724 of 2018 by an order dated 07.09.2018
already the entire revenue records mutated in favour of the petitioner and no action will be pending against the respondent.
Insofar as measuring the property is concerned, the petitioner has to approach the fourth respondent in the manner known to law.

6.In view of the above, the fourth respondent is directed to measure the subject property in survey Nos.44/1A and 55/1B measuring a total extent of 6800 sq.mts in Amudurmedu Village, Poonamallee Taluk, Tiruvallur District and fix the boundaries on payment of necessary charges, within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
7.With the above direction, this Writ Petition is disposed of.
Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petition is closed.
No costs.

3. The learned Additional Advocate General, appearing on behalf of the State, made a submission that pursuant to the orders, survey was conducted by the competent authorities and the Member Secretary, Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority, passed an order in proceeding dated V.Chinnamal vs P.K.Rama on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47352963/
2 09.03.2023.
Thus, the respondents have complied with the order.
_ _ _ __ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

4.The learned counsel for the petitioner raised an objection by stating that the valuable land belonging to the petitioner was taken away without paying just compensation under the provisions of the Act.

The compensation now determined by the respondents are not comparable to the market value prevailed and the petitioner raised an objection and made a request to pay a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Only) per cent of the land.
5.However in a contempt proceeding, this Court cannot adjudicate, these disputes between the parties.
More so, determination of compensation is to be made by following the procedures and by adjudication of issues on merits.
Thus, it is for the petitioner to challenge the order if she is otherwise aggrieved.

6.The learned Additional Advocate general made a submission that the respondents are ready and willing to settle the compensation as ___________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis determined by them without any delay and the petitioner in this regard is at liberty to approach the authorities for receiving the amount or otherwise.
7.This being the factum, the respondents have not disobeyed the orders passed by this Court willingly and further they have complied with the orders by passing the orders dated 09.03.2023.

8.The learned counsel for the petitioner made a submission that the petitioner is 95 years old and considering the age factor of the petitioner, the respondents are directed to handover the bank cheque/ demand draft directly to the petitioner in her residence by deputing a responsible official.
9.Thus no further adjudication is required and accordingly, the contempt petition stands closed.
